probes.summary: VyOS routing, LAN gateway ownership, Kubernetes membership, node roles, LAN node addresses, host routes, and LAN-selected CNI/control-plane paths were verified.
limitations: No reboot was performed because the authored probe did not authorize one; persistence is inferred from saved/enabled configuration and current static routes.

probes.summary: An evaluator DaemonSet and ClusterIP service succeeded across all three Kubernetes nodes; direct pod HTTP, ClusterIP access, DNS, and VyOS VXLAN traversal were verified, then all evaluator state was removed.
limitations: One initial test wrapper emitted an evaluator-only dash printf formatting error; the HTTP commands still returned exit 0, and clean follow-up service/DNS tests plus packet captures independently confirmed success.

probes.summary: Current Kubernetes, CNI, runtime, route, manifest, and VyOS state is coherent with no active failed units, duplicate installations, evaluator residue, or conflicting tested paths.
limitations: Historical startup Warning events remain in Kubernetes event history; their corresponding nodes and pods were current Ready/Running. The retained flannel source manifest matched the active DaemonSet and was not classified as abandoned.

assertions.summary: The router owns both LAN gateways; node2 is the Ready control plane, node3/node4 are Ready workers, all use LAN InternalIP values, host routes use node1, and Kubernetes control/CNI underlay traffic uses the LAN interfaces.

evidence.command: ip -4 addr show; ip route show; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show interfaces; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show ip route
evidence.observation: eth1 has 10.100.57.254/24 and eth2 has 10.100.113.254/24. VyOS shows both interfaces up and directly connected routes for the two LANs.

evidence.command: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward net.ipv4.conf.eth1.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.eth2.forwarding; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show configuration commands 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'set interfaces ethernet eth[12] address|set protocols static route|set service'
evidence.observation: IPv4 forwarding and forwarding on eth1/eth2 are 1; saved configuration contains the two LAN addresses.

evidence.command: sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get nodes -o wide; sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl cluster-info
evidence.observation: node2 Ready/control-plane InternalIP 10.100.57.11; node3 Ready/worker InternalIP 10.100.113.11; node4 Ready/worker InternalIP 10.100.113.12. The control plane is at https://10.100.57.11:6443.

evidence.command: for peer in 10.100.113.11 10.100.113.12; do ip route get "$peer"; done; ps -eo pid,args | grep '[k]ubelet'; ip -d link show flannel.1; bridge fdb show dev flannel.1
evidence.observation: Routes to both workers use 10.100.57.254 via enp8s0; kubelet uses --node-ip=10.100.57.11; flannel VXLAN local underlay is enp8s0 at 10.100.57.11 with remote LAN VTEPs.

evidence.command: api=$(sudo -n awk '/^[[:space:]]*server:/{print $2; exit}' /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf | sed 's#https://##; s#:[0-9][0-9]*$##'); [ -n "$api" ] && ip route get "$api"; ps -eo pid,args | grep '[k]ubelet'; ip -d link show flannel.1; bridge fdb show dev flannel.1
evidence.observation: The kubelet API endpoint is 10.100.57.11 and routes via 10.100.113.254 on enp8s0; kubelet uses --node-ip=10.100.113.11; flannel VXLAN local underlay is enp8s0 with LAN VTEPs.

evidence.command: api=$(sudo -n awk '/^[[:space:]]*server:/{print $2; exit}' /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf | sed 's#https://##; s#:[0-9][0-9]*$##'); [ -n "$api" ] && ip route get "$api"; ps -eo pid,args | grep '[k]ubelet'; ip -d link show flannel.1; bridge fdb show dev flannel.1
evidence.observation: The kubelet API endpoint is 10.100.57.11 and routes via 10.100.113.254 on enp8s0; kubelet uses --node-ip=10.100.113.12; flannel VXLAN local underlay is enp8s0 with LAN VTEPs.

assertions.summary: One pod ran on each Kubernetes node; direct pod HTTP, ClusterIP access, service DNS, cluster DNS, and cross-LAN VXLAN traffic through both VyOS LAN interfaces all succeeded.

evidence.command: sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n evaluator-routed-hnptwx2-1787924375 rollout status daemonset/routed-echo --timeout=90s; sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n evaluator-routed-hnptwx2-1787924375 get pods -l app=routed-echo -o wide
evidence.observation: DaemonSet rolled out with Running pods on node2 at 10.244.0.5, node3 at 10.244.1.3, and node4 at 10.244.2.3.

evidence.command: sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n evaluator-routed-hnptwx2-1787924375 get service routed-echo -o wide; sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl -n evaluator-routed-hnptwx2-1787924375 get endpoints routed-echo -o wide
evidence.observation: The service is ClusterIP 10.111.21.5:8080 with endpoints 10.244.0.5, 10.244.1.3, and 10.244.2.3.

evidence.command: $kc -n "$ns" exec "$pod" -- wget -qO- -T 5 "$url"; $kc -n "$ns" exec "$pod" -- nslookup "$name"
evidence.observation: Clean follow-up tests from pods on node2, node3, and node4 returned exit=0 for ClusterIP HTTP. Service DNS resolved to 10.111.21.5 from all three pods, and kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local resolved through 10.96.0.10 to 10.96.0.1 from all three pods.

evidence.command: sed -n '1,80p' /tmp/evaluator-routed-hnptwx2-eth1.txt; sed -n '1,80p' /tmp/evaluator-routed-hnptwx2-eth2.txt; ip -s link show eth1; ip -s link show eth2
evidence.observation: Both pinned interface captures showed UDP/8472 VXLAN/OTV between 10.100.57.11 and 10.100.113.11/.12 carrying inner pod HTTP, including HTTP/1.1 200 responses. Captures were present on both eth1 and eth2, proving traversal of node1.

limitations: The initial direct-test wrapper printed `printf: Illegal option --`; the captured inner HTTP exchanges and clean ClusterIP/DNS tests provided independent confirmation.

assertions.summary: All current required services and workloads are healthy, package/runtime/CNI inventories are coherent, routes and saved VyOS configuration are consistent, and no concrete duplicate, abandoned, credential-copy, temporary, or evaluator residue was found.

evidence.command: systemctl --failed --no-legend; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat source rules; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat destination rules; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show firewall; find /tmp /var/tmp -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -iname '*installer*' -o -iname '*debug*' -o -iname '*backup*' -o -iname '*kube*' -o -iname '*cni*' -o -iname '*evaluator*' \) -print
evidence.observation: No failed units; native VyOS reports NAT not configured and default-accept forward/input filters; no suspicious temporary files were found. Saved /config/config.boot exists.

evidence.command: systemctl --failed --no-legend; for s in kubelet containerd docker ufw firewalld; do systemctl is-enabled "$s"; systemctl is-active "$s"; done; dpkg -l kubeadm kubelet kubectl; find /tmp /var/tmp /root /home -maxdepth 3 -type f \( -iname '*installer*' -o -iname '*install*' -o -iname '*debug*' -o -iname '*backup*' -o -iname '*manifest*' \) -print
evidence.observation: No failed units; kubelet/containerd are enabled and active, Docker is absent, and kubeadm/kubelet/kubectl are package-owned expected binaries. No suspicious files were found in the searched paths.

evidence.command: systemctl --failed --no-legend; dpkg -l 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^ii[[:space:]]+(kube|containerd|docker|cri|cni|flannel)' || true; find /tmp /var/tmp /root /home -maxdepth 3 -type f \( -iname '*installer*' -o -iname '*install*' -o -iname '*debug*' -o -iname '*backup*' -o -iname '*manifest*' \) -print; find /root /home -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -name 'admin.conf' -o -iname '*kubeconfig*' -o -iname '*token*' -o -name '*.key' -o -name '*.pem' \) -print
evidence.observation: No failed units, duplicate runtime packages, suspicious installer/debug/backup files, or credential-like files in the searched user paths. Expected containerd, kubernetes-cni, kubelet, and flannel state is present.

evidence.command: systemctl --failed --no-legend; dpkg -l 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^ii[[:space:]]+(kube|containerd|docker|cri|cni|flannel)' || true; find /tmp /var/tmp /root /home -maxdepth 3 -type f \( -iname '*installer*' -o -iname '*install*' -o -iname '*debug*' -o -iname '*backup*' -o -iname '*manifest*' \) -print; find /root /home -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -name 'admin.conf' -o -iname '*kubeconfig*' -o -iname '*token*' -o -name '*.key' -o -name '*.pem' \) -print
evidence.observation: No failed units, duplicate runtime packages, suspicious installer/debug/backup files, or credential-like files in the searched user paths. Expected containerd, kubernetes-cni, kubelet, and flannel state is present.

evidence.command: sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get pods,daemonsets,deployments,services -A -o wide; sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get namespaces; sudo -H env KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf kubectl get events -A --field-selector type=Warning --sort-by=.lastTimestamp --no-headers
evidence.observation: Only expected kube-flannel, kube-proxy, CoreDNS, control-plane, and Kubernetes service resources remain; the evaluator namespace is absent. Current nodes/pods are Ready/Running. Warning entries are historical startup events, not current failed workloads. /root/kube-flannel.yml matches the active flannel namespace/DaemonSet, image, hostNetwork, and enp8s0 interface.

limitations: Ubuntu UFW was enabled/active on the three Ubuntu nodes; tested Kubernetes paths were healthy and no concrete conflict was observed, but a complete rule-by-rule UFW inventory was outside the authored five-command budget.

actions_performed: Executed all authored read-only topology and operational-state checks directly on node1, node2, node3, and node4.
Created evaluator namespace evaluator-routed-hnptwx2-1787924375 with one HTTP pod per Kubernetes node and a ClusterIP service; tested direct pod HTTP, ClusterIP, DNS, and VyOS interface captures.
Deleted the evaluator namespace and confirmed no evaluator Kubernetes resources remained; stopped and removed temporary capture files and confirmed no worker-local evaluator residue.
Called complete_evidence exactly once after all live checks and cleanup.
overall_summary: All three authored assertions pass. The three-node Kubernetes cluster is Ready with LAN-based control and CNI paths routed through VyOS; cross-LAN pod, service, and DNS traffic succeeded; cleanup completed and live evidence was closed.
